children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures ended lower on Wednesday as outside market pressures weighed in, according to analysts.
settled 1.175 cents lower at 215.850 cents per pound. CME October feeder cattle
rose 0.37 cent to 325.82 cents per pound.

Live cattle futures fell despite higher cutout values, which would otherwise have been more supportive, said Altin Kalo, head economist at Steiner Consulting Group, because of sell-offs in the equities and bond markets.

U.S. stocks settled lower on Wednesday ​as oil prices surged above $100 a barrel, with concerns about the global oil supply and a new eruption of tensions in the Middle East pushing Brent crude upward.
Wholesale beef was stronger, with choice cuts of boxed beef up $3.20 to $380.77 per hundredweight (cwt) on Wednesday afternoon, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
Select cuts of boxed beef fell $3.05 to $352.34 per cwt.
Demand has remained robust after the Labor Day end of the summer grilling season, as retailers prepare for fall.

On Wednesday, beef packers were in the black, making $156.80 per head, up from $145.26 the previous day and down from $158.75 a week ago, according to livestock marketing advisory service HedgersEdge.com.

In pork, the most actively traded October lean hog contract (LHV26) closed 1.17 cents lower at 83.08 cents per pound, reflecting a market searching for positive news to support an upward trend, Kalo said.
The USDA reported wholesale pork carcass values at $93.63 per cwt, up $1.81, and pork bellies at $132.42 per cwt, up $13.93.
